claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- US and Denmark reach deal over Greenland after Trump annexation threats: Trump says the agreement will give the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland", though specifics have not been confirmed by Danish officials.
- Trump says he is banning CNN and Politico from White House: The US president has had a tense and fiery relationship with the US media throughout his political career.
- Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.
- Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill: The bill is named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch advocate of aid for Ukraine.
- Russian hybrid attacks against Europe intensifying, says Macron: The French president says he has tasked the government with protecting critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.
- Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa: Dineo Motapane is one of nine recent victims whose deaths have left a nation traumatised over the level of violence against women.
- At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.
- Saudi Arabia issues first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthis escalated attacks: Residents later received the all-clear after explosions were reported in the capital.
- Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says he had no doubt she deliberately killed her children: It is the first time the juror, who refused to side with the others and acquit Clancy, has spoken publicly about his decision.
- Shots heard as police start moving migrants from Ceuta beaches: Police reportedly fired into the air on Friday morning as they struggled to contain crowds jostling to secure a place at the tented site.
- Ryanair boss Michael O'Leary apologises over 'high-fare rapists' remarks: O'Leary described his choice of language as "careless" and said "it won't happen again".
- North Korean anthem played for South Korea at Asian Games: Organisers have apologised for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team at the Asian Games in Japan.

image_provider.prompt: A massive wall or barrier made of fractured glass and concrete blocks, fragmenting and shattering outward from a central point of impact. Dark grays and blacks dominate, with red cracks spreading like fissures. The composition is explosive and destabilizing, with jagged shards suspended mid-fall. The style is brutalist and stark, emphasizing rupture, breaking of norms, and systems under strain. Heavy, ominous shadows. No figures—only the abstract violence of structures collapsing inward and outward simultaneously.
